purpose: Every load-bearing claim this command center makes, with the SOURCE probe that produced it and the mechanically independent VERIFIER that checked it. A claim with no source probe is zero signals, not one (rules/common/single-signal-verification.md, rule 6).

claims.claim: The catalog holds every row of the register snapshot: 103 items, 69 open, split A-toolchain 32 / HARNESS 10 / MONITOR 19 / B-workflow_design 8.
claims.source_probe: tools/command-center/seed.py parsing command-center/sources/REGISTER.md by section and id prefix
claims.verifier_probe: register_parse.counts_by_prefix() reproduces the register's own header sentence ('OUTSTANDING 69 / DELIBERATELY-SKIPPED 3 / SUPERSEDED 5 / SETTLED 26') from the table rows WITHOUT reading that sentence -- tests/test_validate.py::test_parser_reproduces_the_registers_own_header_counts

claims.claim: Every item in the catalog is reachable from a final disposition: no dangling dependency, no cycle, no dead end, no phantom owner gate.
claims.source_probe: python tools/command-center/validate.py -> SUCCESS:cc-validate items=103 open=69 reachable=all
claims.verifier_probe: Seventeen mutated-catalog tests prove each check can go RED (dangling dep, cycle, closed-depends-on-open, dead end, phantom gate, evidence-free disposition, dropped item, tampered snapshot, blank register digest, deleted register digest, stale graph, duplicate id, malformed id, empty catalog). A green detector never shown red measures nothing -- and, as CC-11 records, neither does one that was only ever shown a WRONG input and never a MISSING one.

claims.claim: The dependency graph cannot drift from the catalog.
claims.source_probe: catalog.build_graph is the only producer; every close.py verb regenerates it
claims.verifier_probe: validate.py V-GRAPH compares the committed file against a fresh derivation and is proved to fire on a hand-mutated edge_count

claims.claim: Closing an item costs the same one command as opening one.
claims.source_probe: close.py exposes --open and a bare close as single argv forms of the same shape
claims.verifier_probe: tests/test_close.py::test_close_is_one_command_like_open opens a new item and closes it, each in one call, asserting the end disposition

claims.claim: The register gate can never loop: it returns allow for every Stop-family event and for any re-entrant trigger.
claims.source_probe: RegisterGateModule._run early-returns unless event is UserPromptSubmit or SessionStart (agent-self/harness/modules.py)
claims.verifier_probe: test_register_gate.py drives Stop / StopFailure / SubagentStop, a stop_hook_active trigger on both accepted events, a fixed-point test feeding the gate its own injected text back as a prompt, and a 50-event loop-bound test asserting exactly one injection

claims.claim: The gate fires on a stale catalog and is silent on a clean one, including the clean-partial case where only the matching program's items are closed.
claims.source_probe: both-states table executed in test_register_gate.py against the real catalog and two mutated copies
claims.verifier_probe: clean-partial is the sharp control: closing ONLY the 19 MONITOR items must silence the monitor prompt while 50 other items stay open, which proves the gate tracks these items rather than 'the file is non-empty'

claims.claim: The gate's firing rate is 2.4 fires per 20-prompt session -- at the calibration peer and far under the wallpaper line.
claims.source_probe: corpus replay of all 375 owner prompts in _USER-PROMPTS.md through the real predicate (tools/command-center/measure_rate.py)
claims.verifier_probe: NOT YET RUN in a live session. The replay applies no per-item session cooldown and no calibrated-silence gating, both of which only subtract, so the measured number is an UPPER bound on the real rate.
claims.evidence: see MEASURED-RATE in the PR body; stage-2 of the ladder requires >=20 real sessions in the shadow sink before promotion
claims.settling_experiment: collect 20 distinct session_hash values in ~/.agents/state/harness/shadow/ and recompute fires / distinct sessions

claims.claim: The gate's advice is useful -- it surfaces the RIGHT item.
claims.evidence: The shadow sink records {ts, gate, tier, event, reason_code, session_hash} and NO payload (module-modes.json:3), so no measurement of advice quality exists or can exist today.
claims.settling_experiment: Add truncated+redacted injected text to shadow_log() (module-modes.json:41 _next_experiment), then score fires against subsequent close.py --evidence calls via register_item_closed_after_fire. Until then the gate may not be promoted past advise.

claims.claim: R-A02 (the 13-file command-center ledger) and R-H03 (reachability computable) are fully closed by this PR.
claims.source_probe: the 13 files exist under command-center/ and validate.py answers the reachability question
claims.verifier_probe: reading each item's full text: R-A02 also requires the freeze/snapshot clean-room baseline, which is NOT built; R-H03 also requires 11-CAPABILITY-PRESERVATION-GRAPH.json and the 10-DEPENDENCY-GRAPH.* names under the continuation root, which are NOT written
claims.evidence: Both stay OPEN with a --note recording the partial. Claiming either as closed would be the overclaim failure class, which measured 5 of 8 refutations on this estate.

claims.claim: The live ~/.agents/harness tree now carries this gate.
claims.evidence: This lane wrote only to the repo, which is the source of truth. No deploy was run: sync-from-live.ps1 is forbidden here and install.py was not run in deploy mode.
claims.settling_experiment: install.py --check, or a sha256 compare of agent-self/harness against ~/.agents/harness

claims.claim: REACH-6 could be switched off by deleting a single field, and the gate would still print SUCCESS. Fixed 2026-08-13: validate.py now fails closed when provenance.register_sha256 is missing or empty.
claims.source_probe: in-process -- validate.validate() over deepcopies of the real catalog: register_sha256='' gave 0 violations and the key deleted gave 0 violations, while the control (one hex character flipped) gave 1 and provenance={} gave 1. The baseline was clean first, so this was not a dirty tree. Probe: scratch/integrate_reach6_blank_probe.py
claims.verifier_probe: out-of-process -- the real CLI graded on process EXIT CODE against a tmp catalog passed with --catalog, run UNCHANGED in both states: before the fix blank and deleted both exited 0 printing 'SUCCESS:cc-validate items=103 open=58 reachable=all'; after the fix both exit 1, while good stayed 0 and the wrong-digest control stayed 1. Probe: scratch/integrate_reach6_cli_redproof.py
claims.evidence: tests/test_validate.py::test_detects_a_blank_register_digest, ::test_detects_a_deleted_register_digest, ::test_cli_fails_closed_on_a_blank_register_digest -- registered as TI-9. Red-proofed in a throwaway `core.autocrlf=false` clone (the LF bytes ubuntu-latest checks out), with the pre-fix state taken from git HEAD rather than hand-reverted: exactly those three fail there (3 failed, 23 passed) and all 26 pass against the fixed file, so they are neither vacuous nor Windows-only. Blast radius traced rather than assumed: this short-circuit shape occurs at exactly one other site, validate.py:303, which is gated on an explicit CLI flag by design, not on a recorded value -- see CC-12.

claims.claim: V-FIELDS -- 'all 19 Prompt Two fields resolve per item', listed as a check in validate.py's own docstring -- is enforced in CI.
claims.source_probe: validate.py:303 runs V-FIELDS only `if unresolved and require_complete`, and grep over .github/workflows/*.yml, tools/command-center/*.py and command-center/*.py returns the flag's definition (:340) and plumbing (:85, :303, :367) and NO caller. quality.yml:436 invokes `python tools/command-center/validate.py` bare.
claims.verifier_probe: ran the flag directly -- `python tools/command-center/validate.py --require-complete` -> 'work_unit_fields_unresolved=0 work_unit_fields_from_defaults=1133', SUCCESS. A check that reports 0 unresolved is one nobody has been paying for, which is consistent with it never having run.
claims.evidence: Found while tracing CC-11's blast radius; deliberately NOT fixed here. Adding `--require-complete` to quality.yml:436 is free TODAY (0 unresolved) but quality.yml is the shared file this wave was warned about, and the 1133 fields resolving 'from defaults' means the check is weaker than its docstring sentence implies -- whether that is acceptable is the catalog owner's call, not a drive-by from the CI lane.
claims.settling_experiment: already run (see verifier_probe). The remaining open question is a decision, not a measurement: accept 1133 default-resolved fields and wire the flag, or tighten the defaults first.

claims.claim: accept() with no minimum argument enforces REQUIRED_MIN; a mutation of that constant must fail a test that omits minimum=.
claims.evidence: M-IMPL-DEFAULT-ZERO and M-REV-DEFAULT-NINETY-NINE kill the default-floor tests; see command-center/receipts/CC-0014.json

claims.claim: A test that only passes minimum= explicitly does not protect REQUIRED_MIN; mutating the default must SURVIVE it and register a hole.
A test with no mutation record is UNPROVEN and must not count toward any coverage total.
claims.evidence: test_empty_list_rejected_at_explicit_one binds UNPROVEN; coverage_summary reports protected_claims=0 not 100 percent
